title: Story and video pipeline
summary: Datoms, story graph, Hyperlab export, prebaked scenarios and the stills gate.
bodyHtml:
The game records what happens to its people as a story and turns the moments that matter into shot requests. Full detail: docs/video-pipeline.md.

Story layer (src/story/, pure TypeScript)

  • Datoms (datoms.ts): an append-only [entity, attribute, value, tx, added] log with as-of queries and history.
  • Character datoms (characters.ts): character, prop and environment specs; ordered looks give visual versions and slot keys such as state_variants/wounded-v2.
  • Datom mutations (mutations.ts): chronicle diffs two game states into typed mutations (join, death, departure, turning, wound, heal, maim, fog, costume, prop-gained, look) and a beat with stakes. Life-altering ones are flagged.
  • Recorder (recorder.ts): chronicles every choice into the log; saved with the game.
  • Story graph (graph.ts): beats to a hyperlab.sequence v2 file with entities bound to datoms, state snapshots and transitions.
  • Shots (shots.ts): a prompt, up to 9 reference slots, duration, and a cache key per participant look.
  • Hyperlab export (hyperlab.ts): the ordered REST plan.

src/game/ never imports src/story/; test/story.test.ts enforces it.

Two routes to video

  1. Local pre-baked (primary): curated scenarios rendered on the lucifer-comfy worker through Hyperlab's H3 reference-to-video manifest scripts. Free per clip.
  2. fal realtime or bulk (secondary): the H3 Max API through a local proxy. Costs money, off by default, mock-tested only.

The 3D cinematic is always the fallback. A late or broken clip lets the game carry on.

Prebaked scenarios

Three short scenarios cut from seeded engine runs (tools/video/scenarios/defs.ts): the stranger who is bait, a night death with a departure fork, and a companion who turns. 19 shots, about 114 seconds, 60 reference stills. test/story.test.ts fails if content moves the pins; tools/video/scenarios/search.ts finds fresh ones.

H3 reference-to-video on lucifer

tools/video/h3-manifest.ts writes manifests matching Hyperlab's apply_h3_manifest.ps1: service comfy-workflows/MiniMax_H3_R2V, 864x480, at most 6 reference images per shot, prompts in the integrated multimodal form with spoken lines as attributed dialogue. Transition shots open on the old state and end on the new.

Stills approval gate

Reference stills are created as unqueued jobs and must be approved in Hyperlab and bound to datom slots by hand before manifests can be resolved (tools/video/hyperlab-export.ts --resolve). Base slots come first (hero, front_view, three_quarter); later looks are image edits of the approved hero so the face stays put. Every live step is behind an explicit flag and defaults to a dry run.

Commands

npm run video:export -- --scenario stranger-trap
npm run video:bake
npm run video:server -- --mock

In the browser, the URL hash chooses the video mode (#video=mock, #video=baked@..., #video=realtime@...); Backquote opens the debug panel. Code: web/src/video/.

Open items to verify live

Listed at the end of docs/video-pipeline.md: Ether REST bodies, still-job capability names, slot binding, R2V params, pinning to lucifer, fal response keys.
